title: How Much Does a Loyalty Program Cost? (2026)

facts.fact: Loop's pricing page lists its full destination platform starting at $5,000 per year, according to the vendor's own page.
facts.quote: Loop lists the [full destination platform from $5,000 per year](https://loop.fans/pricing).

facts.fact: The page states that Loop's standalone AI Trip Planner has separate pricing and is included in the full destination platform.
facts.quote: Its standalone AI Trip Planner has separate pricing and is included in the full destination platform.

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative single-café model, the owner estimates 300 active members; the page says this is a model, not a typical result or a Loop price quote.
facts.quote: Suppose a café estimates 300 active members.

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative café example, the owner expects 30 reward redemptions a month, each with a $2 marginal cost.
facts.quote: Assume, purely for illustration, that the owner expects 30 redemptions a month at a $2 marginal cost each

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative café example, staff administration is assumed at two hours a month at $25 per hour.
facts.quote: two hours of staff administration at $25 an hour

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative café example, software and messaging are assumed to cost $40 a month.
The page's illustrative café example calculates an estimated monthly program cost of $150, made up of $60 rewards, $50 staff time and $40 tools.
facts.quote: The estimated monthly cost is $150: $60 for rewards, $50 for staff time and $40 for tools.

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative café example, each additional visit is assumed to contribute $6 of gross margin.
facts.quote: If each additional visit contributes $6 of gross margin, 20 visits contribute $120

facts.fact: The page advises that a low software fee can be expensive if setup and manual administration are high.
facts.quote: A low software fee can be expensive if setup and manual administration are high

facts.fact: The page lists the metrics to track for a loyalty program: eligible audience, joining rate, first action, active members, redemptions, and the chosen business outcome.
facts.quote: Track the eligible audience, joining rate, first action, active members, redemptions and the chosen business outcome.

facts.fact: The page recommends a monthly budget check that compares the forecast with actual software fees, issued points, redeemed rewards, and staff time needed to run the program.
facts.quote: Compare the forecast with actual software fees, issued points, redeemed rewards and the staff time required to run the program.

facts.fact: The page advises separating rewards that have been earned from rewards already redeemed, because a large outstanding points balance may represent a future cost.
facts.quote: Separate rewards that have been earned from rewards already redeemed: a large outstanding points balance may represent a future cost.

facts.fact: The page advises that if a reward costs more than the contribution it creates, the rule should be revised or the benefit made experiential rather than increasing the software budget.
facts.quote: If a reward costs more than the contribution it creates, revise the rule or make the benefit experiential rather than increasing the software budget.
